Question: What is wrong with the American Abrams tank, and why are the Ukrainians losing them?
Old_Answer: There are some things wrong with the Abrams tank, despite the endless optimism. Reading most other answers, one would think that the Abrams was perfectly suited for modern operations in Ukraine against drones, despite being designed for fighting in Germany in 1980s against other tanks. There are in fact flaws to the design, the tank has strengths and weaknesses. The most and most obvious thing that’s wrong with the Abrams, is that it is too heavy. It is a really heavy tank, and due to excessive eating it has only gained weight since 1980. The tank was designed originally at 55t, due to attempts at adding more armor to the tank and other upgrades, the M1A2 Sepv3 is estimated to sit at around 73t. The engine compartment has not gotten bigger. Even the older models without DU armor are heavy vehicles. And it has many disadvantages, firstly it does not fit on to the common 50t railroad flat bed cars, which is a logistical problem. Secondly, it does not do well with heavily muddied areas because its ground pressure is massive. Thirdly, it is unable to cross some bridges due to weight limits. Fourthly, the weight means that components of the Abrams require more maintenance and is under more stress than on lighter tanks. Finally, the heavy tank is difficult to tow for other tanks, meaning only a few specialized recovery vehicles can do it. All this weight unfortunately, has not gone where it is needed most, which is the top. Despite around 15t of additional protective upgrades, none of the M1 Abrams ever received anything to make them more difficult to destroy from the top. This means the original M1 Abrams and the newest M1 Abrams are equally vulnerable to drones, DPICM and other top attack weapons. The already excessive weight might also be one of the reasons why no one has added additional armor to the top in the form of cages. The M1 is not a bad tank, but it has design flaws, it was not build to do what it is doing now, it could be better, in fact a drastically different design would be a better option than just adding more weight on this tank. There are several other comparative disadvantageous of the Abrams to some of its competitors, but I think this is enough to point out why it might not feel so hot right now. But wait, 4 FAB-500, that’s like 2000kg of bomb, while 1 FAB-3000 is 3000kg of bomb, shouldn’t that destroy 50% more? No, you see, explosive power is not linear. What does this mean? Well for example 500kg of TNT would produce an incident pressure of around 10 PSI at 100m from detonation site. While 1500kg of TNT would produce an incident pressure of around 18 PSI at 100m from the detonation site. 300% more TNT gives you just 80% more pressure at 100m. Pressure is what collapses buildings, and is the most notable effect of bombs on video. 500kg of TNT creates 18 psi at 70m. So by this logic, if we want to cover an area with 18 PSI blast waves of TNT. 3 bombs with 500kg of TNT could cover an area of 46,000m2 while 1 bomb with 1500kg could cover an area of just 31,000m2. So you can see despite being the same amount of bomb, the more but smaller bombs is actually better at destroying something by area. However, there is more to this, this is just the primary blast effect. We also have the secondary blast effect, we can call this kinetic penetration using delivery body, or we can call it shrapnel. The Bombs are encased in steel, the FAB-3000 has only 1400kg of explosive filler, the rest is steel. When the bomb explodes the steel casing tends to go flying with an initial velocity of about 2,300m/s if my calculations using HMX is right. I know it’s more difficult to see on a still, but if you look below, you can see smoke and dust come out of this building on the eastern side, it is also quite apparent coming out on the western side of the building on the left. That’s not a incident pressure, that is fragmented steel traveling through a dusin layers of wall, and creating additional impact shrapnel through each wall inside those rooms. This building is still standing, but the inside is completely shredded, though this is not so obvious from the air. Finally, we have the ODAB variant. These bombs spread an explosive aerosol over an area then detonates it, this has the massive advantage that the aerosol can get inside buildings and other areas like bunkers or buildings, before detonating. This exponentially increases their ability to demolish, as well as almost guaranteeing termination of all life in the area, no matter what kind of cover is provided. No ODAB-3000 exists as far as I am aware. Due to their function thermobaric explosives scale a lot better than conventional ones do, and can cover massive areas with their aerosols if there is enough of it. The Russian FOAB would probably be an ODAB-7000, at this scale the FOAB allegedly provides the power of 44t of TNT, which is twice as much as the Davy Crocket mini nuclear weapon. Let’s hope we don’t see the use of such weapons.
